articles.title: ANTHROPIC PREVIEWS A UNIVERSAL DRIVER LETTING CLAUDE CONTROL ANY LAB OR FACTORY HARDWARE
articles.summary: Anthropic opened a research preview of the Model Hardware Standard (MHS), a shared driver spec that lets AI agents discover and operate lab and manufacturing instruments, microscopes, liquid handlers, robotic arms, and laser systems through a single interface instead of the bespoke, vendor-specific integrations that normally take weeks or months to build. The driver uses simple read/write primitives any device can implement, plus natural-language tags that capture physical characteristics (like a robot arm's weight) that used to live only in paper manuals or an engineer's head, giving the agent everything it needs.

articles.title: PERPLEXITY AND NVIDIA UNVEIL "PORTABLE COMPUTER" FOR OFFLINE LOCAL AI EXECUTION
articles.summary: Perplexity has partnered with Nvidia to launch Portable Computer, an agentic Computer platform designed to execute advanced AI agent workflows entirely on-device without continuous cloud API dependency or recurring token costs. Powered by Nvidia's compact edge silicon architecture, the system runs quantized local inference models to process multimodal search, complex reasoning, and persistent agentic tasks directly at the edge.

articles.title: NVME 2.4 SPECIFICATION ADDS POST-QUANTUM CRYPTOGRAPHY AND GRANULAR POWER MANAGEMENT
articles.summary: The NVM Express organization has released the NVMe 2.4 specification, integrating quantum-resistant encryption algorithms and advanced telemetry to address future-proofed enterprise security and datacenter energy constraints. These enhancements formalize a critical hardware-level bridge between next-generation flash controllers and high-efficiency datacenter storage architectures.

articles.title: ADVANCED PACKAGING AND THERMAL BOTTLENECKS COMPLICATE HIGH-LAYER HBM SCALING
articles.summary: As high-bandwidth memory (HBM) architectures scale to 12-high and 16-high vertical DRAM stacks, semiconductor packaging faces severe physical limits across thermal dissipation, mechanical stress, and die warpage. Thinner DRAM silicon substrates required to maintain JEDEC package height profiles exacerbate through-silicon via (TSV) structural fatigue and increase susceptibility to micro-cracking during thermal cycling. The escalating complexity and defect density risks underscore that packaging and thermal reliability—rather than pure lithography—now dictate the economic scaling and memory bandwidth roadmap for frontier AI hardware accelerators.

articles.title: ROS2SMOLVLA: DEPLOYING VLA MODELS ON AN INDUSTRIAL CO-BOT
articles.summary: ROS2SmolVLA is an open-source ROS 2 interface that deploys Hugging Face's lightweight SmolVLA model directly onto an industrial Universal Robots UR10e arm for local, vision-guided pick-and-place. If you have been playing with an SO-101 arm and would like to graduate up to controlling an industrial co-bots, this looks like a great starter solution.

articles.title: NVIDIA COMPASS: CROSS-EMBODIMENT ROBOT NAVIGATION POLICY
articles.summary: NVIDIA just dropped a new tutorial on COMPASS, an agent-assisted residual reinforcement learning framework designed to adapt pretrained X-Mobility locomotion policies to different robotic platforms (such as Boston Dynamics' Spot). It offers developers a powerful methodology to reuse general navigation and locomotion skills across varied physical platforms, vastly reducing the time and cost required to train new hardware embodiments from scratch.

articles.title: SIFIVE DEBUTS BIGSKY 2U SERVER PLATFORM WITH 32 P870-D RISC-V CORES
articles.summary: BigSky SF-2U870 is an enterprise-grade 2U rackmount development platform designed to accelerate RISC-V datacenter software validation and workload porting. Built around 32 high-performance P870-D cores clocked at 2.0 GHz, the system features full compliance with the RVA23 profile standard alongside support for 256 GB of DDR5-5600 memory, 64 PCIe Gen 5 lanes across four x16 slots, and dual U.2 NVMe storage. In addition to running enterprise distributions like Ubuntu 26.04 LTS and RHEL 10 out of the box, the platform can act as an accelerated host node, running Nvidia CUDA workloads directly on RISC-V hardware ahead of future NVLink Fusion integration.

articles.title: ROS 2 PACKAGES FOR ROBOTIQ ADAPTIVE GRIPPERS
articles.summary: Robotiq's official, first-party ROS 2 driver release for its 2F-85 and 2F-140 adaptive grippers brings optimized C++ SDK communication, Modbus-cycle grouping for 200 Hz control, and integrated hardware simulation. This release is critical for commercial integrators, as transitioning from community drivers to official manufacturer support guarantees long-term driver stability, API safety, and reliable end-effector control.

articles.title: AMAZON TO DEPLOY 2 MILLION NVIDIA GPUS ACROSS GLOBAL DATA CENTER FLEET
articles.summary: Amazon is set to purchase two million Nvidia graphics processing units for its global data center infrastructure over the next two years to support frontier AI model training and cloud inference workloads.

articles.title: ANTHROPIC SIGNS $45 BILLION INFRASTRUCTURE DEAL WITH NSCALE FOR VERA RUBIN COMPUTE
articles.summary: Anthropic has entered into a six-year, $45 billion cloud computing agreement with London-based infrastructure provider Nscale to secure 460 megawatts of dedicated capacity at the Monarch campus in Mason County, West Virginia.

articles.title: AMAZON HIKES HARDWARE PRICES UP TO 60% CITING AI-DRIVEN MEMORY SHORTAGES
articles.summary: Amazon has raised retail pricing across its consumer hardware portfolio by as much as 60%, citing severe cost inflation for memory and storage components driven by enterprise AI infrastructure demand.

articles.title: PLAUD UNVEILS PLAUD ONE AI EARBUDS WITH BUILT-IN 4G LTE CONNECTIVITY
articles.summary: Plaud has announced the Plaud One Explorer Edition, a $250 pair of true wireless AI earbuds paired with an eSIM-enabled 4G LTE charging case designed for standalone voice capture and agentic task execution without a paired smartphone.
